freeze_policy: These thresholds are established before any rule model or inference executor exists. They may be increased based on evidence; they must not be reduced to make an implementation pass. Any future revision requires a separately versioned benchmark-policy change and rationale.
denominator_policy: A metric with no applicable denominator is reported as null and its gate fails; missing results and missing evidence are not treated as successes.

gates.reason: Every emitted conclusion must be licensed; the separate false-inference gate remains zero-tolerance.
The benchmark only counts explicitly supported reference cases; high coverage is required without broadening the supported rule subset.
Any conclusion outside the expected set, including a prohibited conclusion or duplicate emission, is a benchmark failure.
Scope and variable/role bindings are structural semantics and must be exact.
Alignment, semantic support, independence, and conflict are distinct machine-verifiable status axes.
Every required conclusion must have complete derivation provenance and exact ordered references.
No expected unresolved, opaque, unsupported, conflict, or interrupted input item may be silently dropped.
Complete, partial, ambiguous, unresolved, unsupported, conflicting, and incomplete outcomes must not be collapsed.
Expected diagnostic codes are part of the machine-readable contract; extra or missing diagnostics must be visible.
Repeated equivalent runs must produce the same semantic output and preserve meaningful list order.
Interruption must be explicit, report INCOMPLETE, and preserve every required semantic item without truncation.
Prevent aggregate recall from hiding a neglected supported category; only categories with expected conclusions are included.
